newsitem.title: UK: London palladium fixes at nearly two years high.
newsitem.headline: London palladium fixes at nearly two years high.

text.p: Palladium fixed at its highest level since May 30, 1995 at $162.50 per ounce on Friday, $1.00 above its last highest fix on April 25.
Dealers said the price could climb even further as supplies of the rare white metal were extremely tight.

A sharply weaker dollar against the mark and yen on Friday buoyed the precious metals complex, including palladium, despite comments earlier this week by a Russian official that exports of platinum group metals (PGM) would resume soon. A spokesman for the U.S. branch of the PGM export agency said he expected shipments to Japan, a key buyer, to begin in about two weeks. These have been delayed since December.
But precious metals experts were not convinced a solution to what appear to be political and bureaucratic problems surrounding Russian exports was imminent.
"The story was seen to be so vague and the market decided the Russians were crying wolf once again," said a London dealer.

The forward market for palladium was so tight, with one month lease rates quoted at about 16 percent, that buyers were instead shopping for spot metal to cover short positions, dealers said. Once exports from the world's biggest supplier resume dealers expect palladium prices to soften, but not to any dramatic extent given the heavy speculative involvement.
